archetypes.name: reference-integrity
archetypes.rationale: The move extracts a large normative block from an always-loaded file into an on-demand reference; any surviving anchor links, cross-references, or 'see ## Execution Issues Tracking' pointers in SKILL.md or sibling files that still target the old section become dangling.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit every occurrence in `skills/implement/SKILL.md` and `skills/implement/references/oos-pipeline.md` of the strings 'Execution Issues Tracking', 'execution-issues-tracking.md', and 'OOS triage policy' to verify every former inline reference now resolves to the new reference file rather than the removed SKILL.md section. Check that the 'Machine reachability' stub added to SKILL.md lists every script that the moved block formerly named (e.g., materialize-manifest-oos.sh, oos-file-conflict-deps.sh, oos-issue-cap.sh) and that no script cited in the removed block was silently dropped. Verify the new `execution-issues-tracking.md` file contains the **Terminal disposition invariant** paragraph that the updated test in `scripts/test-implement-structure.sh` now greps for there. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: call-site-coverage
archetypes.rationale: The section was always-loaded before; it is now on-demand via MANDATORY-READ at Steps 8+/9a.1 only — but earlier steps (Step 2, Step 5, Step 7a) also reference execution-issues.md logging and OOS dual-write without a load directive, so those steps may silently operate without the normative rules.
archetypes.prompt_body: Scan `skills/implement/SKILL.md` for every step (Step 2 through Step 16) that mentions `execution-issues.md`, 'dual-write', 'Pre-existing Code Issues', 'OOS triage', 'oos-accepted-main-agent.md', or 'append-execution-issue.sh'. For each such step, check whether the updated SKILL.md now includes a 'MANDATORY — READ ENTIRE FILE … execution-issues-tracking.md' directive at or before that step, or whether the orchestrator can still reach those steps without ever loading the reference file. Identify any step that instructs the orchestrator to apply a triage gate or dual-write rule but lacks the on-demand load directive, representing a semantic gap introduced by the move. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
